doc.title: Walter Booker and Jimmy Cobb interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995

title: Young players, history and new instruments
summary: Booker says young players now build on jazz history; Cobb notes electric drums and synthesizers, and they joke about a free amp.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: You know I think it’s been a misnomer in the last 20 years or less maybe, for jazz players to come up and think that there is going to be a change in the music without dealing with what was—
Yeah, the history, see? So now I think recently it’s, we can see a lot of young guys coming up and these young guys are thinking about the music—

Like the best music has already been played because they are realizing and they are approaching it like that is the school of thought. That is the basis, the background by which, you know, the base on which this music should be built. Now it is going to its own time, we’re letting time be the thing that determines how it is being expressed and not trying to play something different then what it was. You know what I mean? And of course time will do it because it sounds, the instruments will help time do it, for the way they’re making instruments, the way they make new drums.

Well not only that, they’re making electric drums, and that’s a sound that you didn’t hear before, and that’s going to have to take you someplace else. And then they’re making these synthesizers, I can’t even say that word. You’ve got all this stuff that really charges the music up.
Yeah you better watch it, you won’t get a free amp or something.
Yeah you better cut this off right here. Could you delete that section?
